record.paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
record.original_question: Which quality characteristics of machine-learning models, beyond accuracy or confusion matrices, should be defined and evaluated for safety-critical systems, including resource behavior, time behavior, robustness against adversarial examples, analyzability or interpretability, and testability for formal verification?

evidence.quote: In order to use machine-learning models in safety-critical systems, it is necessary to define and evaluate models by the performance indicators from various perspectives besides accuracy. If we refer to the software quality model [20], then accuracy (confusion matrix), resource behavior (required memory), time behavior (execution time), fault tolerance (robustness against Adversarial Examples [22], hereinafter referred to as AE), analyzability (ease of internal visualization or interpretability), and testability (simple model structure advantageous for formal verification) appear to be relevant perspective (performance indicator) to machine-learning models.

artifact.category_tag: ML quality characteristics for safety-critical systems
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a machine-learning model M (for example, a trained classifier or regressor) that is to be deployed as a component of a safety-critical system. Beyond classical predictive accuracy (e.g., confusion-matrix-based metrics), identify and rigorously define a complete set of quality characteristics that should be specified, measured, and evaluated to certify M for safety-critical use. In particular, provide precise mathematical or operational definitions, together with concrete evaluation procedures (metrics, test protocols, and acceptance criteria), for at least the following candidate characteristics:

1. Resource behavior: quantitative measures of the memory footprint required for inference (and, if relevant, training).
2. Time behavior: quantitative measures of inference latency and throughput, including worst-case execution time bounds.
3. Robustness against adversarial examples: given an input space X with a metric d and a perturbation budget ε > 0, define and evaluate the model's resistance to inputs x' with d(x, x') ≤ ε that change the model's output in an unsafe way; specify both empirical attack-based metrics and certified/provable robustness metrics.
4. Analyzability / interpretability: formal notions of the ease with which the internal computations of M can be inspected, visualized, or explained, together with quantitative measures of explanation quality.
5. Testability for formal verification: structural properties of M (e.g., architectural simplicity, piecewise-linearity, bounded depth) that enable tractable application of formal verification methods, together with measures of verification cost and coverage.

Propose a coherent quality model that integrates these characteristics, demonstrate that the proposed definitions are mutually consistent and measurable, and discuss any trade-offs (e.g., between accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and verification cost) that arise when optimizing M with respect to all of them simultaneously.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is an open engineering/research challenge concerning the definition of quality characteristics for safety-critical ML beyond accuracy. It remains an active area of research, with ongoing standardization efforts (e.g., ISO/IEC 25000-series adaptations to ML, ISO/IEC TR 24028, ISO/IEC 5469, and the EU AI Act's high-risk requirements) and a growing literature on robustness, interpretability, and formal verification of neural networks, but no universally accepted, complete quality model has been established.

status_evidence.title: ISO/IEC 5469:2024 — Functional safety and AI systems
status_evidence.snippet: Standard addressing the use of AI in safety-related functions, indicating ongoing standardization rather than a settled solution.
status_evidence.claim: Quality characteristics for safety-critical ML are still being formalized in active international standards work.

status_evidence.title: ISO/IEC TR 24028:2020 — Overview of trustworthiness in AI
status_evidence.snippet: Technical report surveying trustworthiness aspects of AI including robustness, transparency, and reliability without prescribing definitive metrics.
status_evidence.claim: There is no universally agreed quantitative quality model covering all the listed characteristics.
